blocks.text: Tool use is Anthropic's mechanism for letting Claude call external capabilities it does not have built in, checking a live weather service, querying a database, running a calculation, applying the general function calling idea already covered for OpenAI's own equivalent feature to Anthropic's own distinct request and response shape.

This topic covers declaring a tool with its input_schema, the tool_use content block the model returns instead of plain text, sending a tool_result back to continue the conversation, handling multiple tool calls in one turn, the tool_use stop_reason, and how this compares directly to OpenAI's function calling.
1. What Tool Use Is

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: When answering needs an external capability, Claude responds with a tool_use block instead of an ordinary text reply

blocks.text: A request declares one or more tools available for this conversation. When a user's question genuinely needs one of them, checking today's weather rather than something the model could reasonably know on its own, Claude responds not with generated text but with a structured request to call a specific tool with specific arguments.
2. Defining a Tool

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A tool declaration carries a name, a description guiding when to use it, and an input_schema defining its arguments

blocks.text: Each tool is declared with a name, a description that guides the model on when this tool is actually the right one to reach for, and an input_schema, a JSON schema exactly like the ones covered in the earlier Schema-Based Outputs topic, defining exactly what arguments the tool accepts.
3. The tool_use Content Block

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A tool_use block carries a unique id, the tool name, and its parsed input arguments

blocks.text: When Claude decides to call a tool, response.content contains a block with type set to tool_use, carrying a unique id for this specific call, the name of the declared tool being requested, and input, the arguments already parsed as a JSON object matching the input_schema.
4. Executing the Tool and Returning a Result

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: The caller actually runs the tool, then sends the result back referencing the same tool_use id, letting Claude continue

blocks.text: Claude never actually executes anything itself, the caller reads tool_block.input, runs the real weather lookup, and sends the result back as a new message so the conversation can continue with that real information in hand.
5. The tool_result Message Structure

The result is sent back as a user-role message containing a tool_result content block, referencing the original tool_use id through tool_use_id, so Claude knows precisely which pending call this result answers.

code.content:
follow_up = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
    max_tokens=1024,
    tools=tools,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Tokyo?"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": response.content},
        {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": tool_block.id, "content": "18C, partly cloudy"},
        ]},
    ],
)

blocks.text: 6. Handling Multiple Tool Calls

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A single assistant turn can request several tools at once, each needing its own matching tool_result before the conversation continues

blocks.text: A single turn's content array can carry more than one tool_use block if the model decides several independent calls are needed at once, checking weather in two different cities in the same turn, for instance. Every one of them needs its own matching tool_result before Claude will continue.
7. The tool_use Stop Reason

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A stop_reason of tool_use signals Claude is waiting on a result, distinct from a normal end_turn completion

blocks.text: Checking response.stop_reason before assuming a turn is finished matters here specifically, a value of tool_use means Claude is waiting on a result and has not actually finished responding yet, distinct from end_turn, covered generally in the Messages API topic, which means the reply is already complete.
8. Comparing to OpenAI Function Calling

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: The same underlying idea, expressed through a different request and response shape between the two providers

blocks.title: Same Concept, Different Shape
blocks.content: Whichever provider you are integrating, always check its own specific field names rather than assuming the exact structure from one API transfers directly to the other.

blocks.text: 9. When to Reach for Tool Use

Tool use fits any capability Claude genuinely cannot provide from its own training, live data, side effects like sending an email, or precise calculation better done in real code, exactly the same motivating cases covered generally when function calling was first introduced, now expressed through Anthropic's own specific mechanics.
Worked Example

A developer declares a single get_weather tool with an input_schema requiring a city string, then sends a user question asking about the weather in Tokyo. Claude responds with stop_reason set to tool_use and a single tool_use block naming get_weather with input set to city: Tokyo.

The developer calls a real weather API with that city, gets back 18C, partly cloudy, and sends it back as a tool_result referencing the original tool_use id. Claude's next reply arrives with stop_reason set to end_turn and a natural-language answer incorporating the real weather data.
Common Mistakes

items: Sending a tool_result without referencing the exact tool_use_id it answers
Treating a tool_use content block as if it were ordinary generated text meant to be shown to the user directly
Not checking stop_reason for tool_use before assuming a turn has fully completed
Writing a vague input_schema that leaves the model guessing at argument names or types

blocks.text: Practice

Declare a calculate tool accepting two numbers and an operator through its input_schema. Send a question requiring arithmetic, extract the tool_use block's input, compute the real result yourself, and send it back as a tool_result to get Claude's final natural-language answer.
Key Takeaway

Tool use lets Claude request an external capability through a tool_use content block naming a declared tool and its parsed input, with the caller executing the real work and returning a tool_result referencing the same id to continue the conversation, the same underlying idea as OpenAI's function calling, expressed through Anthropic's own distinct content-block structure.
